newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA, ROMANIA TO RENEW TALKS ON DANUBE BRIDGE.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA, ROMANIA TO RENEW TALKS ON DANUBE BRIDGE.

text.p: Bulgaria and Romania signed on Thursday a protocol to renew negotiations by the year-end over building a new Danube river bridge following disagreements over its location for years.
"This is a new dialogue after a year-long stillness of negotiations over the bridge location," Bulgaria's Transport Minister Stamen Stamenov told reporters after signing the protocol.
Romania's state secretary Tudorel Florescu signed the protocol, which envisages to resume talks between the two sides within 30 days.
Florescu is in Sofia for a conference of transport ministers from the Central European Initiative and the Black Sea Economic Cooperation.

Stamenov pinpointed that traffic flow between the two countries has diverted after lifting the oil and trade embargo, imposed by the United Nations in May 1992 for Belgrade's involvement in the Bosnian war.
"We will start evaluating all aspects of the links between Bulgaria and Romania," Stamenov said.

A feasibility study by a British firm Sir Alexander Gibb indicated that the western position that Bulgaria prefers would be more suitable and recommended in the first place a link between Bulgaria's Lom port and Romania's village of Rast.

Bulgaria insisted on a bridge linking the port of Vidin and the Romanian town of Calafat near the Serbian border. Romania prefered to connect Turnu-Maguerele with Bulgaria's Nikopol, halfway on the two countries' 600 km (480 miles) Danube River border.
Stamenov said the two sides would also consider a location between Oryahovo in Bulgaria and the Romanian town of Bechet.
The new bridge, intended to ease Europe's access to the East, is estimated to cost more than $400 million. It will be part of the European Union's trans-European network.
The two countries are now connected by only one congested bridge and operate two ferry links across the Danube River.
